einzeiler: Alexander faces Persia's Great King in the historic Battle of Issus.
kurzfassung: Alexander consolidates control over Asia Minor through lightning-fast campaigns and successful sieges. The campaign culminates in the decisive Battle of Issus, where Alexander defeats Darius III's massive royal army. This historic victory opens the door to total conquest, marking a pivotal turning point in ancient history.
stichpunkte: Alexander sends Persian armor to Athens as propaganda, deliberately excluding Sparta.
Rapid marches through Anatolia exhaust the army but yield key city surrenders.
Alexander disbands his fleet and relies on land-based operations to neutralize Persian naval advantage.
The grueling siege of Halicarnassus showcases Alexander's superior engineering and tactical flexibility.
A severe illness and bounties on his head highlight the constant dangers facing the young conqueror.
Darius III marches a massive royal army northward, leading to an inevitable clash at Issus.
The Battle of Issus features a dramatic confrontation between Alexander and Darius.
Darius flees the battlefield, leaving behind his royal camp, family, and immense wealth.
Alexander's chivalrous treatment of the captured Persian royal women highlights a complex character.

Aftermath and the Spoils of War

clips.text: Troops changing allegiance instantly upon seeing their former emperor demonstrate deep institutional loyalty rather than personal familiarity.
Historical timelines often misrepresent a siege duration by assuming a month-long operation simply because it occupied a month on a calendar.

clips.hook: The ancient history of siege warfare
clips.text: Prehistoric armies utilized various methods to conquer walled settlements, from starvation and scaling ladders to underground tunneling and battering rams.

clips.hook: Ostentatious opulence of the royal army
clips.text: Elite imperial units displayed staggering wealth through golden necklaces, jeweled tunics, and elaborate garments rather than practical combat gear.

clips.hook: The grim reality of ancient casualty ratios
clips.text: Victors and losers suffered vastly different casualty numbers, with the overwhelming majority of fatalities occurring during the post-battle rout.

beschreibung: The stage is set for an in-person showdown between Alexander and Persia's Great King. The resulting Battle of Issus, although often ignored by Hollywood, is one of the most important battles in all ancient history. It gets its due here.
